variations.name: Amine solvent capture (incumbent licensors plus next-gen low-energy amines)
variations.description: Flue gas is bubbled through liquid amine solutions that chemically bind CO2 and release it when heated, the benchmark capture route used in nearly every operating commercial CCS plant today.

companies.name: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries
companies.what: Most-deployed post-combustion licensor (KM CDR Process, ~15+ commercial plants incl. Petra Nova) with next-gen low-energy KS-21 solvent selected for Drax BECCS and multiple UK/US FEEDs.
companies.signal: Petra Nova restarted 2023; KS-21 in commercial FEEDs through 2025

companies.name: Shell (CANSOLV)
companies.what: CANSOLV amine system running at SaskPower Boundary Dam since 2014 and selected for Net Zero Teesside Power, the first gas-CCGT-with-capture FID (Dec 2024).
companies.signal: Boundary Dam ~1 Mtpa design; NZT Power under construction

companies.name: SLB Capturi
companies.what: SLB-majority JV (ex-Aker Carbon Capture tech) that delivered Brevik CCS, the world's first industrial-scale cement capture plant (400 ktpa), opened June 2025 with CO2 shipped to Northern Lights.
companies.signal: Brevik operating since mid-2025; Hafslund Celsio waste-to-energy contract won 2025

companies.name: Aker Carbon Capture ASA
companies.what: Former standalone Oslo-listed capture pureplay; folded its technology into the SLB Capturi JV (2024), then sold its remaining 20% stake (NOK 1.83B, 2025) and is being liquidated.
companies.signal: 20% stake sold to Aker ASA May 2025; shareholder cash-out and liquidation

companies.name: Fluor
companies.what: Econamine FG+ amine licensor (dozens of gas-processing references); capture provider for the $2B Project Tundra coal retrofit, now stalled after TC Energy's exit and no FID.
companies.signal: Project Tundra in limbo since Dec 2024 despite $350M DOE award

companies.name: BASF
companies.what: OASE blue low-energy amine solvent licensed globally for flue-gas capture, typically delivered through EPC partners such as JGC and Samsung E&A.
companies.signal: Multiple commercial licenses across gas treating and flue gas

companies.name: Axens
companies.what: Licenses IFPEN's DMX demixing (two-phase) solvent that cuts regeneration energy, demonstrated on steel-mill gas at ArcelorMittal Dunkirk in the EU 3D project.
companies.signal: DMX industrial demo operated 2023-2025

companies.name: Carbon Clean
companies.what: APBS-CDRMax solvent plus CycloneCC rotating packed beds that shrink absorber columns ~10x for skid-mounted industrial retrofits.
companies.signal: $150M Series C led by Chevron (2022); first industrial CycloneCC hit 4,000 hours at Fertiglobe Abu Dhabi, TRL7 (Apr 2025)

companies.name: ION Clean Energy
companies.what: Water-lean ICE-31 amine demonstrating 98-99% capture on gas-fired flue at TCM/NCCC; capture technology for Calpine's 1.75 Mtpa Sutter gas-plant decarbonization project.
companies.signal: $45M Series A led by Chevron New Energies (Apr 2024); DOE cost-share signed for Sutter

companies.name: Entropy Inc.
companies.what: Advantage Energy spinout running modified-amine capture on natural gas plants; Glacier Phase 1 (32 ktpa) operating since 2022, Phase 2 ($127M, 160 ktpa) targeted Q2 2026.
companies.signal: C$200M Canada Growth Fund investment plus first carbon contract-for-difference; US$300M Brookfield commitment

variations.name: Non-amine solvents (potassium carbonate, chilled ammonia, amino acids, ionic liquids, enzyme-catalyzed)
variations.description: Alternative liquid chemistries (hot potassium carbonate, ammonia, enzymes, alkali hydroxides) absorb CO2 with cheaper, non-degrading, non-toxic solvents, trading some kinetics for lower lifetime cost and cleaner emissions.

companies.name: Capsol Technologies
companies.what: Oslo-listed licensor of Hot Potassium Carbonate end-of-pipe capture that needs no steam tie-in; technology behind Stockholm Exergi's BECCS plant (FID March 2025, under construction).
companies.signal: Holcim took a strategic equity stake in 2025 after CapsolGo demo at Dotternhausen; Saipem co-development agreement

companies.name: KC8 Capture Technologies
companies.what: Australian UNO MK3 potassium carbonate process with precipitating absorption, targeting cement and lime; PACER project at Cement Australia Gladstone and solvent testing at the US NCCC.
companies.signal: A$5.4M Australian CCTP grant for ReDeFINE demo facility; LETA co-investment

companies.name: Baker Hughes
companies.what: Owns the Chilled Ammonia Process for low-pressure flue gas (cement, WtE, refineries) alongside acquired rotating-bed and MOF capture lines.
companies.signal: CAP commercially offered; broader CCUS portfolio expanding via Chart acquisition (closing mid-2026)

companies.name: Saipem
companies.what: Bluenzyme: carbonic-anhydrase enzyme-catalyzed carbonate solvent capture sold as pre-engineered 200 t/d plug-and-play units for small and medium emitters.
companies.signal: Bluenzyme 200 product line launched Sept 2023; first sales in EU

companies.name: CO2 Solutions
companies.what: Quebec pioneer of enzymatic CO2 capture that ran a 30 t/d unit at a pulp mill; entered insolvency in 2019 and its assets were bought by Saipem, becoming the basis of Bluenzyme.
companies.signal: Assets acquired by Saipem 2019 after creditor protection

companies.name: C-Capture
companies.what: University of Leeds spinout with an amine-free organic solvent claiming lower cost and no toxic emissions; XLR8 CCS compatibility trials at Heidelberg Materials cement, Glass Futures/Pilkington glass, and Energy Works Hull.
companies.signal: UK NZIP-backed multi-site trials running 2024-2025 with Wood as engineering partner

companies.name: CarbonFree
companies.what: Alkaline capture-to-mineral SkyCycle process turning flue CO2 into precipitated calcium carbonate; commercial plant built with U.S. Steel at Gary Works, Indiana.
companies.signal: SkyCycle Gary Works plant constructed 2024-2025 under offtake with U.S. Steel

companies.name: RTI International
companies.what: Non-profit developer of a non-aqueous solvent (NAS) with materially lower regeneration energy, piloted at Technology Centre Mongstad and SINTEF facilities.
companies.signal: DOE-funded TCM campaigns completed; licensing-stage technology

variations.white_space: Ionic liquids and amino-acid salts still have no venture-scale champion - viscosity, solvent cost, and oxygen degradation have kept them in the lab - so the field is effectively three chemistries (HPC, ammonia, enzyme); an opening exists for oxygen-tolerant, dirt-cheap solvents for dirty flue gases and for a second enzymatic player beyond Saipem.

variations.name: Solid sorbent capture (MOF/zeolite filter beds, VPSA/TSA cycles)
variations.description: Porous solids such as MOFs and amine-functionalized particles soak up CO2 from flue gas and release it with modest heat or vacuum swings, promising lower energy use and no liquid solvent emissions.

companies.name: Svante
companies.what: Structured laminate filter cartridges (incl. CALF-20 MOF) cycled in a rotating TSA contactor; opened the world's first carbon capture filter gigafactory (Redwood, Burnaby) in May 2025.
companies.signal: US$318M Series E led by Chevron (2022); $145M gigafactory commissioned; investors incl. GE Vernova, Samsung, Temasek, Canada Growth Fund

companies.name: Nuada (formerly MOF Technologies)
companies.what: Belfast company running MOF-based vacuum pressure swing adsorption that cuts capture energy up to 90%; pilots live at enfinium energy-from-waste and a biomass site, with cement and US lime partnerships.
companies.signal: EIC Accelerator EUR 2.5M (Apr 2025) plus BGF £3.4M; two pilot plants operating

companies.name: Kawasaki Heavy Industries
companies.what: KCC moving-bed system using solid amine sorbent regenerated by ~60C waste-heat steam; 40 t/d demonstration on real coal flue gas at Kansai Electric's Maizuru plant.
companies.signal: 5 t/d in-house facility plus 40 t/d utility demo since 2023

companies.name: Verdox
companies.what: All-electric electro-swing adsorption (quinone electrodes) needing no heat or steam; demonstrated capture from ~1% CO2 aluminum smelter off-gas with Hydro at Sunndal (Nov 2025).
companies.signal: $80M from Breakthrough Energy Ventures et al. (2022); pilot unit commissioned Oct 2025, first demo unit targeted 2027

companies.name: Mosaic Materials
companies.what: UC Berkeley spinout whose diamine-appended MOF 'molecular sponge' adsorbents were acquired by Baker Hughes (2022) to anchor its next-gen sorbent capture line.
companies.signal: Acquired by Baker Hughes, April 2022

companies.name: TDA Research
companies.what: Colorado developer of low-cost alkalized-alumina and supported-amine sorbents with multiple DOE-funded slipstream pilots on coal and gas flue gas.
companies.signal: Serial DOE awards through 2025; pilot campaigns at NCCC

companies.name: Promethean Particles
companies.what: Nottingham-based continuous-flow MOF manufacturer scaling tonne-per-day production of capture sorbents for filter beds, including trials on industrial flue slipstreams.
companies.signal: £8M Series A (2023); UK flue-gas MOF trials

variations.name: Membrane separation (polymeric and hybrid membrane-cryogenic)
variations.description: Selective polymer films let CO2 permeate faster than nitrogen or methane, separating gases with electricity alone - no steam, solvents, or chemicals - and pair naturally with cryogenic polishing for high purity.

companies.name: MTR Carbon Capture
companies.what: Polaris membrane developer that completed the world's largest membrane capture plant (150 t/d, ~55 ktpa, 99.9% liquid CO2) on coal flue gas at the Wyoming Integrated Test Center.
companies.signal: DOE large-pilot completed Oct 2024 and operating 2025; selected for cement (Holcim) DOE demo

companies.name: Air Liquide
companies.what: Runs commercial hybrid membrane-plus-cryogenic capture (CryoCap H2) on SMR hydrogen offgas at Port-Jerome since 2015 and sells Medal CO2 membranes for gas processing.
companies.signal: CryoCap commercial reference >100 ktpa; global membrane franchise

companies.name: Honeywell UOP
companies.what: Separex membrane systems are a decades-old workhorse for bulk CO2 removal in natural gas sweetening, with hundreds of installed units worldwide.
companies.signal: Mature commercial fleet in gas processing

companies.name: Evonik
companies.what: SEPURAN Green hollow-fiber membranes commercially separate CO2 from methane in thousands of biogas upgrading installations, the largest deployed membrane-CO2 fleet.
companies.signal: Thousands of biogas references; capacity expansions through 2025

companies.name: Aqualung Carbon Capture
companies.what: Norwegian NTNU-heritage facilitated-transport membranes operating without feed compression, piloted on natural gas processing, lime kilns, and waste-to-energy flue gas.
companies.signal: Closed Phase 1 of 2025 financing with a top-3 global membrane maker, LGE, Tupras Ventures and Delek (Apr 2025)

companies.name: Ardent Process Technologies (formerly Compact Membrane Systems)
companies.what: Delaware company whose Optiperm fluoropolymer membranes deliver fully-electrified, chemicals-free capture; paid pilot rigs running at voestalpine (steel), RHI Magnesita (refractories), and OMV (petrochemicals).
companies.signal: Three paid industrial pilots delivered 2024-2025; Series A ~$16.5M (2023)

variations.white_space: At 4-15% CO2 flue concentrations membranes need multi-stage compression, so they lose to solvents on energy at large scale - hence few players; the opening is hybrid membrane-cryogenic trains, steam-less retrofits at mid-size sites, and high-CO2 industrial streams (biogas, ethanol, gas processing) where membranes already win.

variations.name: Cryogenic capture (CO2 desublimation/frost)
variations.description: Flue gas is chilled until CO2 freezes out as solid frost or condenses to liquid, yielding ultra-pure, pipeline-ready CO2 using only electricity and refrigeration hardware instead of chemical solvents.

companies.name: Chart Industries
companies.what: Owns Cryogenic Carbon Capture (CCC) desublimation technology (from SES acquisition) and the cryogenic boxes, tanks, and liquefiers used across the CO2 chain.
companies.signal: Being acquired by Baker Hughes for $13.6B all-cash, closing targeted mid-2026; shareholder approval secured

companies.name: Sustainable Energy Solutions
companies.what: BYU spinout that invented the CCC desublimation process demonstrating ~30% energy savings vs amines on coal/cement slipstreams; bought by Chart in December 2020.
companies.signal: Acquired by Chart Industries, Dec 2020

companies.name: Carbon America
companies.what: Vertically-integrated developer whose FrostCC freezes CO2 from flue gas (99% capture, 99.97% purity in 1,000-hour NCCC pilot) while self-developing CCS at three Colorado ethanol plants (~525 ktpa).
companies.signal: NCCC pilot completed 2024; first standard commercial module in fabrication

companies.name: REVCOO
companies.what: French startup capturing CO2 by cryogenic separation of flue gas into liquid CO2 onsite, targeting cement and lime kilns with containerized units.
companies.signal: Seed-stage; industrial pilot with French lime/cement partners

companies.name: Air Liquide
companies.what: CryoCap family applies cryogenic purification and liquefaction to high-CO2 streams (H2 PSA tail gas, oxyfuel flue), the commercial anchor of cryogenic capture today.
companies.signal: Commercial since 2015 at Port-Jerome

variations.white_space: Physics keeps the field thin: refrigeration energy penalties and dry-ice fouling only pencil where CO2 is concentrated or cold is cheap, so credible players cluster around ethanol/biogas and hydrogen tail gas; an opening exists in coupling capture to LNG regasification cold and in steam-less modular units for sites with no boiler.

variations.name: Oxy-fuel combustion and Allam-Fetvedt supercritical CO2 power cycles
variations.description: Burning fuel in pure oxygen instead of air produces an exhaust of nearly pure CO2 (no nitrogen to separate), making capture inherent to the combustion or power cycle itself.

companies.name: NET Power
companies.what: Commercializing the Allam-Fetvedt supercritical CO2 gas power cycle with 100% inherent capture; 50 MWth La Porte demo ran since 2018, utility-scale Project Permian in detailed design.
companies.signal: NYSE: NPWR; Permian re-baselined to $1.7-2.0B with ~2029 COD, FID targeted H2 2026; late-2025 pivot to gas-turbine-first hybrid strategy; facing investor class action

companies.name: 8 Rivers
companies.what: Inventor and licensor of the Allam-Fetvedt cycle and related inherent-capture processes (8RH2 hydrogen, Cormorant), monetizing via project development and licensing.
companies.signal: SK Inc. majority investment ($100M, 2022); restructured 2024 to focus flagship projects

companies.name: thyssenkrupp polysius
companies.what: Built the polysius pure oxyfuel demonstration kiln (450 t/d clinker) for the Catch4Climate consortium at Schwenk's Mergelstetten plant, the first dedicated oxyfuel cement line.
companies.signal: Demo kiln commissioned 2025 for Buzzi/Dyckerhoff, Heidelberg, Schwenk, and Vicat

companies.name: Heidelberg Materials
companies.what: Cement major co-funding the Catch4Climate oxyfuel demo and developing full oxyfuel kiln conversions in parallel with its operating Brevik amine plant.
companies.signal: Multiple capture routes funded across EU plants

companies.name: Clean Energy Systems
companies.what: Rocket-engine-derived oxy-combustors for carbon-negative biomass (BECCS) power; flagship Mendota, CA project with Chevron/Microsoft/SLB announced 2021 has stalled with no construction progress made public since.
companies.signal: $15M Series A led by Carbon Direct (2021); Mendota BECCS shelved

companies.name: Linde
companies.what: Supplies the air separation units, oxyfuel burners, and CO2 processing units that underpin oxy-combustion retrofits in cement, glass, and steel.
companies.signal: Global ASU fleet; multiple oxyfuel cement/glass trials

variations.white_space: ASU capex and whole-plant redesign make this a consortium-only game, and NET Power's cost reset shows the FOAK penalty; the opening is licensing standardized pure-oxyfuel kiln conversions for cement and lime where a near-pure CO2 stream slashes downstream capture cost to compression-only.

variations.name: Pre-combustion and inherent-capture routes (gasification, chemical looping, molten carbonate fuel cells)
variations.description: CO2 is separated before or during fuel conversion - from concentrated syngas in hydrogen/ammonia plants, via oxygen-carrier solids in chemical looping, or inside molten carbonate fuel cells - where high CO2 partial pressure makes capture far cheaper than from dilute flue gas.

companies.name: Air Products
companies.what: Operates SMR capture at Port Arthur (~1 Mtpa since 2013) and is building the $7B+ Louisiana blue hydrogen complex with >5 Mtpa CO2 capture and sequestration.
companies.signal: Louisiana complex under construction; 2025 portfolio pruning under new CEO kept blue H2 flagship

companies.name: Shell
companies.what: Quest has captured >1 Mtpa from Scotford hydrogen units since 2015; FID taken on Polaris (2024) to add ~650 ktpa from refinery/chemicals process gas.
companies.signal: Quest ~9 Mt cumulative; Polaris under construction

companies.name: Topsoe
companies.what: SynCOR autothermal reforming licensor enabling ~95-99% capture-ready blue hydrogen and ammonia, selected for major US Gulf Coast projects.
companies.signal: Multiple blue H2/ammonia license wins 2023-2025

companies.name: Johnson Matthey
companies.what: LCH ATR/GHR low-carbon hydrogen technology chosen for EET Hydrogen's HPP1 at Stanlow, the UK's first large blue hydrogen plant in the HyNet cluster.
companies.signal: HPP1 in delivery as HyNet reached financial close milestones 2024-2025

companies.name: FuelCell Energy
companies.what: Molten carbonate fuel cells that strip >90% of CO2 from another plant's flue gas while cogenerating power and hydrogen; joint pilot with ExxonMobil live at the Esso Rotterdam refinery since July 2025, CO2 to Porthos storage.
companies.signal: NASDAQ: FCEL; restructured 2024-2025 to cut cash burn; Rotterdam is first industrial CFC capture test

companies.name: Babcock & Wilcox
companies.what: BrightLoop chemical looping (Ohio State heritage) splits fuels into hydrogen/steam with inherently separated CO2; commercial-scale Massillon, Ohio facility and Black Hills Energy Wyoming project advancing.
companies.signal: Funding Massillon partly via asset divestitures (2025) amid balance-sheet strain; $16M Wyoming grant

companies.name: Sinopec
companies.what: Built China's first megaton CCUS chain at Qilu-Shengli (1 Mtpa, operating since 2022), capturing from coal-to-hydrogen tail gas via liquefaction purification for EOR.
companies.signal: 1 Mtpa operating; 109 km dense-phase CO2 pipeline

variations.white_space: Gasification/reforming capture is scaling fast, but chemical looping and carbonate fuel cells each have effectively one committed champion (a financially strained B&W; Exxon/FuelCell's single pilot) because solids circulation and stack durability at scale are unproven - validation at Rotterdam or Massillon would open room for licensing-model fast followers.

variations.name: Calcium looping and indirect calcination for cement/lime kilns
variations.description: Lime-based or molten-salt sorbents absorb CO2 at kiln temperatures, or limestone is calcined in an externally heated vessel, releasing pure process CO2 - approaches purpose-built for cement and lime where two-thirds of emissions come from the rock itself.

companies.name: Calix / Leilac
companies.what: Externally-heated steel-tube calciner that separates pure process CO2 without solvents; LEILAC-1 piloted at Lixhe, and LEILAC-2 demonstration is a JV with Heidelberg Materials relocated to Ennigerloh, Germany, targeting ~2026 commissioning.
companies.signal: ASX: CXL; EUR 16M Horizon 2020 grant retained; licensing revenues forecast from 2027; pre-FEED completed Sept 2025

companies.name: Origen
companies.what: ZerCaL oxy-fired flash calciner producing zero-carbon lime with CO2 captured at source; ZerCaL250 commercial demonstrator with Singleton Birch in the Humber, plus a North Dakota lime-DAC build.
companies.signal: $13M Series A led by Barclays Climate Ventures (Jan 2025)

companies.name: Mantel Capture
companies.what: MIT spinout using molten borate salts that capture CO2 at ~600C inside boilers and kilns while returning high-grade heat, roughly halving the energy penalty; first industrial demo at Kruger's Wayagamack pulp mill (mid-2025).
companies.signal: $30M raised; FEED started Dec 2025 for commercial-scale SAGD project in Alberta

companies.name: Heidelberg Materials
companies.what: Industrial anchor for indirect calcination as Leilac-2 JV partner and host plant owner, alongside its portfolio of amine and oxyfuel capture builds.
companies.signal: Brevik CCS operating; Leilac-2 hosted at its Ennigerloh plant

variations.white_space: Kiln integration risk plus cement's decade-long capital cycles deter startups, leaving roughly three credible technology owners worldwide; the nearer opening is lime (smaller kilns, purer limestone, simpler retrofit) and electrically heated calciners that double as flexible load - a slot Calix only partially occupies.

variations.name: Modular small-emitter capture (containerized units, building exhaust, gensets)
variations.description: Factory-built, skid- or container-sized capture units (typically 1-100 kt/yr) cut site engineering to weeks, opening capture to waste-to-energy plants, gas engines, buildings, and other emitters too small for bespoke megaprojects.

companies.name: SLB Capturi
companies.what: Just Catch standardized 40-100 ktpa modular amine plants; Twence waste-to-energy unit handed over Jan 2025 and five Just Catch 100 units at Orsted's Kalundborg BECCS hub (430 ktpa) operational early 2026.
companies.signal: Repeat modular orders incl. Hafslund Celsio (2025); first mover in serial production

companies.name: Carbon Clean
companies.what: CycloneCC containerized rotating-packed-bed units installable in under a week; 285 t/d C1 series factory-tested at commercial scale (May 2025) and partnership with MODEC for offshore FPSO capture.
companies.signal: First industrial unit ran 4,000 hours at Fertiglobe; TRL7

companies.name: CarbonQuest
companies.what: Distributed capture for buildings, data centers, and onsite power that liquefies CO2 in basements and sells it into concrete; six commercial deployments led by NYC multifamily towers.
companies.signal: $20M growth round led by Riverbend Energy Group (Feb 2025)

companies.name: Entropy Inc.
companies.what: Repeatable modular capture skids for gas-fired engines and turbines at gas plants - Glacier Phase 2 retrofits nine engines plus a turbine for 160 ktpa total.
companies.signal: $127M Phase 2 FID; Canada Growth Fund carbon offtake underpins revenue

companies.name: Capsol Technologies
companies.what: CapsolGo containerized demonstration units and CapsolEoP end-of-pipe plants for mid-size WtE/bioenergy emitters, run without steam integration.
companies.signal: CapsolGo demo completed at Holcim Dotternhausen 2025; multiple EU licenses

companies.name: ION Clean Energy
companies.what: ICE Blocks: pre-engineered modular capture product line launched for smaller emission sources using the ICE-31 solvent.
companies.signal: Product launch Aug 2025

companies.name: Saipem
companies.what: Bluenzyme 200 pre-engineered enzymatic skid (200 t/d) marketed as plug-and-play for small and medium industrial emitters.
companies.signal: Industrialized product line since 2023

companies.name: Compact Carbon Capture (3C)
companies.what: Norwegian developer of rotating-bed process intensification for small-footprint capture, acquired by Baker Hughes in 2020 as the basis of its modular capture line.
companies.signal: Acquired by Baker Hughes, Nov 2020

companies.name: Carbon Reform
companies.what: Carbon Capsule pods that scrub CO2 from commercial-building HVAC return air, cutting ventilation energy while capturing carbon; early seed stage.
companies.signal: Seed-funded (~$3M); pilot installations with university/commercial partners

variations.white_space: Below ~1 kt/yr (gensets, small boilers) there is still no credible player - parasitic load, footprint, and CO2 logistics destroy economics at that scale - so the open play is capture-as-a-service with centralized CO2 aggregation, viable mainly where the gas has onsite reuse value.

variations.name: Mobile and maritime onboard capture (ships, trucks, locomotives)
variations.description: Compact capture systems ride on the vehicle itself - scrubbing CO2 from ship, truck, or locomotive exhaust and storing it onboard as liquid CO2 or solid carbonate for offload in port or at depots - decarbonizing engines that cannot easily switch fuels.

companies.name: Wartsila
companies.what: Delivered the world's first full-scale marine CCS retrofit (7 MW system on Solvang's ethylene carrier Clipper Eris, ~70% capture, operating since Feb 2025) and launched a commercial OCCS product.
companies.signal: Commercial launch May 2025 at estimated EUR 50-70/tCO2 captured

companies.name: Value Maritime
companies.what: Plug-and-play Filtree scrubber-plus-capture units with onboard 'CO2 battery' tanks offloaded for greenhouse reuse; the largest installed OCCS fleet, including MOL's 75,000 dwt tanker Nexus Victoria (2025).
companies.signal: 10+ vessels equipped across container/tanker fleets; repeat orders from X-Press Feeders and MOL

companies.name: Seabound
companies.what: Calcium-looping pods that convert exhaust CO2 into limestone pebbles onboard; world-first commercial project on cement carrier UBC Cork (Hartmann/InterMaritime), offloading captured limestone to Heidelberg's Brevik plant.
companies.signal: ~$4.4M seed plus grants; commercial deployment launched July 2025 with up to 95% CO2 capture

companies.name: Carbon Ridge
companies.what: Centrifugal (rotating packed bed) onboard capture needing ~75% less space than conventional columns; first centrifugal system at sea on Scorpio Tankers' LR2 STI Spiga (July 2025).
companies.signal: >$20M total funding led by Katapult Ocean and Alfa8 with Berge Bulk participation

companies.name: Mitsubishi Shipbuilding
companies.what: Ran CC-Ocean, the world's first marine-based CO2 capture demonstration on a coal carrier (2021), and is productizing compact onboard capture units for newbuilds.
companies.signal: Demo completed; commercial marine capture units in development

companies.name: Langh Tech
companies.what: Finnish scrubber maker extending closed-loop SOx scrubbers into combined CO2 capture, with pilot units capturing at sea in 2025.
companies.signal: Pilot systems operating on own fleet vessels

companies.name: Calcarea
companies.what: Caltech spinout reacting ship exhaust with limestone and seawater to form dissolved bicarbonate discharged safely to the ocean - eliminating onboard CO2 storage and port offload entirely (up to ~75% capture).
companies.signal: Lomar Labs collaboration; ship-design partnership with Aurelia (2025)

companies.name: STAX Engineering
companies.what: Barge-based at-berth exhaust capture-as-a-service (CARB-approved for all vessel classes); demonstrated first integrated PM/NOx/CO2 capture with Seabound at Port of Long Beach (98% CO2).
companies.signal: $70M raised (Feb 2025); 1,670 vessels serviced in 2025; fleet expanding to 27 barges by 2027

companies.name: Remora
companies.what: Exhaust capture devices for semi-trucks and locomotives capturing up to ~90% (1 t CO2/hr), selling the purified CO2; locomotive pilots with Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern.
companies.signal: $117M total raised incl. $60M Series B led by Valor Equity Partners (2025)

companies.name: Qaptis
companies.what: EPFL spinout retrofitting trucks with waste-heat-driven capture that liquefies CO2 onboard, targeting 90% capture from diesel exhaust.
companies.signal: CHF 1.3M initial round plus FIT seed loan; prototype-to-commercial phase

variations.white_space: Demand hinges on unsettled rules (IMO's net-zero pricing framework and EU ETS credit for captured CO2) and ports almost nowhere offer CO2 reception, so most systems are first-of-kind; trucks and rail are emptier still - Remora is the only well-funded player because weight, duty cycles, and CO2 logistics are brutal - leaving an opening for port/depot-side offload infrastructure and capture-as-a-service models like STAX's.
